Short-grain Italian rice high in amylopectin, ideal for risotto.
Fresh Tuber melanosporum, aromatic and earthy.
Mixed varietal tomatoes with balanced acidity.
Bring vegetable stock to a gentle simmer and keep warm over low heat.
Sweat finely diced shallots in butter until translucent, about 4 minutes.
Add arborio rice and stir to coat, cooking until the edges turn glassy.
Deglaze with white wine and reduce until nearly dry.
Ladle warm stock one cup at a time, stirring until absorbed before the next addition.
Finish off heat with cold butter, grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, and shaved truffle.
Halve tomatoes, toss with olive oil, and roast at 200C for 35 minutes.
Sweat onions and garlic, then add roasted tomatoes and stock; simmer 25 minutes.
Mound flour, make a well, and incorporate eggs and yolks gradually.
Knead 10 minutes, rest 30 minutes, then roll and cut into ribbons.
Whisk olive oil, eggs, and sugar until pale, then fold in flour and zest.
Bake at 175C for 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

task: Create a new form from scratch titled 'Product Feedback - Mobile App'. INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, vote_count, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 1, 2, 'Use SimpleImputer from scikit-learn inside a Pipeline. For pandas-native imputation, df.fillna(df.median()) works well for numeric columns, and df.fillna(df.mode().iloc[0]) for categorical. Wrap it in a ColumnTransformer to apply different strategies per column type.', 87, 1, '2023-02-10 12:00:00', '2023-06-01 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, vote_count, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (2, 2, 5, 'Build a Pipeline with ColumnTransformer. Put pandas-based feature engineering in a FunctionTransformer (with validate=False) and scikit-learn transformers like StandardScaler and OneHotEncoder in the same ColumnTransformer. This keeps everything reproducible and leak-free.', 134, 1, '2023-04-19 09:10:00', '2024-01-15 11:30:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, vote_count, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (3, 3, 1, 'Use OneHotEncoder for low-cardinality nominal features and OrdinalEncoder for genuinely ordinal features. Tree-based models can often handle ordinal encoding of nominal features, but one-hot is safer for linear models. Always fit encoders on training data only.', 62, 1, '2023-06-26 10:45:00', '2023-11-02 14:20:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, vote_count, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (4, 4, 2, 'Use PolynomialFeatures from scikit-learn with interaction_only=True, or generate interactions manually with pandas via df[col_a] * df[col_b] in a loop. For large feature sets, PolynomialFeatures inside a Pipeline is cleaner and handles column naming via get_feature_names_out.', 91, 1, '2023-09-03 08:00:00', '2024-02-20 16:00:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, vote_count, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (5, 5, 3, 'Wrap StandardScaler in a Pipeline and set the output to a DataFrame using set_output(transform="pandas") (scikit-learn >= 1.2). Alternatively, manually reassign df.columns after transform.', 45, 1, '2023-11-15 09:30:00', '2024-01-02 12:00:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, vote_count, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (6, 6, 5, 'Use pandas shift() for lag features and rolling() for window statistics, but always shift the target and align indices to avoid leakage. Then feed the engineered DataFrame into a scikit-learn model via a time-series split.', 58, 1, '2024-01-09 10:15:00', '2024-03-05 09:00:00');

rows: Use SimpleImputer from scikit-learn inside a Pipeline. For pandas-native imputation, df.fillna(df.median()) works well for numeric columns, and df.fillna(df.mode().iloc[0]) for categorical. Wrap it in a ColumnTransformer to apply different strategies per column type.

Build a Pipeline with ColumnTransformer. Put pandas-based feature engineering in a FunctionTransformer (with validate=False) and scikit-learn transformers like StandardScaler and OneHotEncoder in the same ColumnTransformer. This keeps everything reproducible and leak-free.

Use OneHotEncoder for low-cardinality nominal features and OrdinalEncoder for genuinely ordinal features. Tree-based models can often handle ordinal encoding of nominal features, but one-hot is safer for linear models. Always fit encoders on training data only.

Use PolynomialFeatures from scikit-learn with interaction_only=True, or generate interactions manually with pandas via df[col_a] * df[col_b] in a loop. For large feature sets, PolynomialFeatures inside a Pipeline is cleaner and handles column naming via get_feature_names_out.
Wrap StandardScaler in a Pipeline and set the output to a DataFrame using set_output(transform="pandas") (scikit-learn >= 1.2). Alternatively, manually reassign df.columns after transform.

Use pandas shift() for lag features and rolling() for window statistics, but always shift the target and align indices to avoid leakage. Then feed the engineered DataFrame into a scikit-learn model via a time-series split.

INSERT INTO questions (id, user_id, title, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 1, 'Best practices for cross-validation with imbalanced time-series data', 'I am working on a fraud detection problem with highly imbalanced time-series data. What is the best way to set up cross-validation so that I respect temporal ordering while still handling the class imbalance? I have been using stratified KFold but I suspect it leaks future information.', '2024-03-01 10:00:00', '2024-03-01 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO questions (id, user_id, title, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (2, 4, 'How do I handle missing timestamps when resampling a pandas DataFrame?', 'My sensor data has irregular gaps. When I resample to a fixed frequency I get NaNs. Should I interpolate or drop? What are the tradeoffs?', '2024-03-04 13:25:00', '2024-03-04 13:25:00');

INSERT INTO questions (id, user_id, title, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (3, 5, 'Which metric should I use for evaluating imbalanced classification models?', 'Accuracy is misleading on my imbalanced dataset. Should I use ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, or something else?', '2024-03-07 16:40:00', '2024-03-07 16:40:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 1, 2, 'You should avoid stratified KFold for time-series data because it shuffles observations and leaks future information into the training set. Consider using a time-aware splitter such as TimeSeriesSplit from scikit-learn, and combine it with resampling techniques inside the training folds only.', '2024-03-01 15:10:00', '2024-03-01 15:10:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (2, 1, 3, 'In addition to respecting temporal order, make sure any oversampling happens strictly within each training fold. Applying SMOTE before splitting will contaminate your validation set with synthetic points derived from future data.', '2024-03-02 09:30:00', '2024-03-02 09:30:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (3, 2, 1, 'It depends on the downstream use. For interpolation-friendly signals like temperature, linear interpolation is usually fine. For event counts, forward-fill or zero-fill is often safer.', '2024-03-05 10:15:00', '2024-03-05 10:15:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (4, 3, 5, 'For imbalanced problems PR-AUC (average precision) is usually more informative than ROC-AUC because it focuses on the minority class.', '2024-03-08 12:00:00', '2024-03-08 12:00:00');

INSERT INTO comments (id, user_id, question_id, answer_id, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 1, 1, NULL, 'Thanks, I was using stratified KFold and I think that was the source of the leakage I was seeing.', '2024-03-01 16:00:00', '2024-03-01 16:00:00');

INSERT INTO comments (id, user_id, question_id, answer_id, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (2, 4, NULL, 1, 'Does TimeSeriesSplit handle the class imbalance at all, or do you still need resampling?', '2024-03-01 17:20:00', '2024-03-01 17:20:00');

INSERT INTO questions (id, user_id, title, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (3, 4, 'What is the difference between learning_rate and n_estimators in gradient boosting?', 'I keep seeing advice to lower the learning rate and increase the number of trees. Can someone explain the tradeoff clearly?', '2023-06-09 12:10:00', '2023-06-09 12:10:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 1, 2, 'Regularization alone will not stop overfitting if your trees are too deep. The main cause here is likely max_depth. Try reducing max_depth to 3 or 4, and also lower the learning rate while increasing n_estimators. Combine that with early stopping on a validation set.', 1, '2023-06-01 11:30:00', '2023-06-01 11:30:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (2, 1, 1, 'Try reducing max_depth first, then add early stopping with a validation set. Also check whether your 120 features include leakage from the target.', 0, '2023-06-01 13:05:00', '2023-06-01 13:05:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (3, 1, 4, 'You may also want to increase min_child_weight and use a smaller subsample. But depth is the biggest lever in my experience.', 0, '2023-06-01 15:40:00', '2023-06-01 15:40:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (4, 2, 5, 'Use scale_pos_weight = neg/pos as a first pass, and evaluate with AUC-PR rather than accuracy.', 1, '2023-06-05 18:00:00', '2023-06-05 18:00:00');

INSERT INTO answers (id, question_id, user_id, body, is_accepted, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (5, 3, 2, 'Lower learning rate needs more estimators to reach the same fit, but usually generalizes better. It is a bias-variance and compute tradeoff.', 1, '2023-06-09 14:00:00', '2023-06-09 14:00:00');

INSERT INTO comments (id, answer_id, user_id, body, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 1, 1, 'Use early stopping with a validation set and it will stop before overfitting. That said, depth still matters most.', '2023-06-01 12:00:00', '2023-06-01 12:00:00');

rows: Regularization alone will not stop overfitting if your trees are too deep. The main cause here is likely max_depth. Try reducing max_depth to 3 or 4, and also lower the learning rate while increasing n_estimators. Combine that with early stopping on a validation set.
Try reducing max_depth first, then add early stopping with a validation set. Also check whether your 120 features include leakage from the target.
You may also want to increase min_child_weight and use a smaller subsample. But depth is the biggest lever in my experience.
Use scale_pos_weight = neg/pos as a first pass, and evaluate with AUC-PR rather than accuracy.
Lower learning rate needs more estimators to reach the same fit, but usually generalizes better. It is a bias-variance and compute tradeoff.
Use early stopping with a validation set and it will stop before overfitting. That said, depth still matters most.
I agree, reducing max_depth to 3 helped me a lot on a similar dataset.
Also try adding a validation curve over max_depth values to pick the best one.
AUC-PR is definitely the right metric here, thanks.
Why does my XGBoost model overfit despite regularization?

I am training an XGBoost classifier on a dataset with ~5k rows and 120 features. I set reg_alpha=1, reg_lambda=2, subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.8, but the training accuracy is 0.99 while validation accuracy is 0.72. Why is it still overfitting?
How do I handle class imbalance with LightGBM?
My positive class is only 2% of the data. Should I use is_unbalance, scale_pos_weight, or resampling? What works best in practice?
What is the difference between learning_rate and n_estimators in gradient boosting?
I keep seeing advice to lower the learning rate and increase the number of trees. Can someone explain the tradeoff clearly?

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 1, 1, 'Prepare the Room and Subfloor', 'Remove existing flooring and baseboards. Ensure the subfloor is clean, flat, and dry. Check for moisture and level any low spots with a floor leveler.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/floating-floor/step1.jpg', '2024-01-10 10:00:00', '2024-01-10 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (2, 1, 2, 'Acclimate the Hardwood Planks', 'Lay the plank boxes flat in the room for 48-72 hours so the wood adjusts to the room temperature and humidity before installation.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/floating-floor/step2.jpg', '2024-01-10 10:00:00', '2024-01-10 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (3, 1, 3, 'Install the Underlayment', 'Roll out the underlayment over the entire subfloor, overlapping seams by 4-6 inches and sealing them with the manufacturer-approved tape. This provides moisture protection, sound dampening, and a cushion for the floating planks.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/floating-floor/step3.jpg', '2024-01-10 10:00:00', '2024-01-10 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (4, 1, 4, 'Lay the First Row of Planks', 'Start along the longest wall, placing spacers to leave a 1/4-inch expansion gap. Lock the first row together and align the tongue side toward the wall.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/floating-floor/step4.jpg', '2024-01-10 10:00:00', '2024-01-10 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (5, 1, 5, 'Continue Plank Rows and Stagger Joints', 'Continue laying rows, staggering end joints by at least 6 inches between adjacent rows. Use a tapping block and pull bar to close gaps without damaging the planks.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/floating-floor/step5.jpg', '2024-01-10 10:00:00', '2024-01-10 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (6, 1, 6, 'Trim and Finish the Edges', 'Cut planks to fit around doorways and walls using a jigsaw or miter saw. Remove spacers, reinstall baseboards, and add transition strips at doorways.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/floating-floor/step6.jpg', '2024-01-10 10:00:00', '2024-01-10 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (7, 2, 1, 'Prepare the Subfloor', 'Ensure the subfloor is structurally sound, clean, and flat. Install a cement backer board over plywood subfloors.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/tile-floor/step1.jpg', '2024-01-12 10:00:00', '2024-01-12 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (8, 2, 2, 'Apply Thinset and Lay Tile', 'Spread thinset with a notched trowel and set tiles using spacers for even grout lines.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/tile-floor/step2.jpg', '2024-01-12 10:00:00', '2024-01-12 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (9, 3, 1, 'Cut and Assemble the Frame', 'Cut cedar boards to length and assemble the frame with exterior screws and corner brackets.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/garden-bed/step1.jpg', '2024-02-01 10:00:00', '2024-02-01 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (10, 4, 1, 'Prep and Prime the Walls', 'Fill nail holes, sand smooth, and apply a coat of primer to all walls.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/paint-room/step1.jpg', '2024-02-15 10:00:00', '2024-02-15 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO guide_steps (id, guide_id, step_number, title, instructions, image_url, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (11, 5, 1, 'Turn Off Power and Remove the Old Switch', 'Shut off power at the breaker, test for voltage, and remove the existing switch from the wall box.', 'https://images.homedepot.com/guides/dimmer-switch/step1.jpg', '2024-03-05 10:00:00', '2024-03-05 10:00:00');

INSERT INTO item_bank (id, item_code, item_type_id, subject_id, ngss_standard_id, grade_level, stem, answer_key, points, approved, approved_by, approved_at, created_by, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (6, 'SCI8-SA02', 3, 1, 1, 8, 'Describe the role of chloroplasts in photosynthesis.', 'Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis, where light energy is used to convert CO2 and H2O into glucose and O2.', 2.0, 1, 1, '2024-01-15 08:30:00', 2, '2024-01-15 08:30:00', '2024-01-15 08:30:00');

INSERT INTO item_bank (id, item_code, item_type_id, subject_id, ngss_standard_id, grade_level, stem, answer_key, points, approved, approved_by, approved_at, created_by, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (8, 'SCI8-SA04', 3, 1, 1, 8, 'Why is carbon considered a key element in biological molecules?', 'Carbon forms four stable covalent bonds, allowing it to create complex, diverse molecules essential for life such as proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates.', 2.0, 1, 1, '2024-01-15 08:30:00', 2, '2024-01-15 08:30:00', '2024-01-15 08:30:00');

INSERT INTO item_bank (id, item_code, item_type_id, subject_id, ngss_standard_id, grade_level, stem, answer_key, points, approved, approved_by, approved_at, created_by, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (21, 'SCI8-SA05', 3, 1, 1, 8, 'Explain how the structure of a chloroplast supports its function in photosynthesis.', 'The thylakoid membranes contain chlorophyll and are the site of light-dependent reactions; the stroma contains enzymes for the Calvin cycle, allowing efficient conversion of light energy to chemical energy.', 2.0, 1, 1, '2024-01-15 08:30:00', 2, '2024-01-15 08:30:00', '2024-01-15 08:30:00');

rows: Which process produces oxygen in plants?
What is the main product of photosynthesis?
How many ATP molecules are produced during glycolysis?
What is the molar mass of glucose (C6H12O6)?
Explain how photosynthesis and cellular respiration are related in terms of matter cycling.
Photosynthesis converts CO2 and H2O into glucose and O2; cellular respiration breaks down glucose and O2 into CO2 and H2O, conserving matter.
Describe the role of chloroplasts in photosynthesis.
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis, where light energy is used to convert CO2 and H2O into glucose and O2.
How does cellular respiration help maintain energy balance in organisms?
Cellular respiration breaks down glucose to release energy stored in chemical bonds, which is used for cellular work, maintaining homeostasis.
Why is carbon considered a key element in biological molecules?
Carbon forms four stable covalent bonds, allowing it to create complex, diverse molecules essential for life such as proteins, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates.
Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
What is the primary energy source for photosynthesis?
What is the net ATP yield from one glucose molecule in aerobic respiration?
How many carbon atoms are in a molecule of glucose?
What gas is released during photosynthesis?
What is the chemical formula for water?
How many oxygen atoms are in a molecule of CO2?
Which molecule is the primary energy carrier in cells?
What is the main function of stomata in plants?
What is the approximate percentage of oxygen in Earth’s atmosphere?
How many hydrogen atoms are in a water molecule?
Explain how the structure of a chloroplast supports its function in photosynthesis.

The thylakoid membranes contain chlorophyll and are the site of light-dependent reactions; the stroma contains enzymes for the Calvin cycle, allowing efficient conversion of light energy to chemical energy.
How do plants use the glucose produced during photosynthesis?
Plants use glucose for energy (via cellular respiration), build cell walls (as cellulose), store energy (as starch), and synthesize other organic molecules.
Why is the conservation of matter important in ecosystems?
Matter is recycled through biogeochemical cycles; conservation ensures that nutrients are available for organisms to build biomass and sustain life.
How does cellular respiration contribute to the carbon cycle?
It releases CO2 into the atmosphere as a byproduct, which can be reused by plants in photosynthesis, completing the cycle.
